input: Build a capsule wardrobe for the office

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Office dress codes vary enormously — business formal, business casual, creative casual — which dictates the entire category of clothing to include.
Knowing whether this is a full wardrobe rebuild or filling gaps in an existing wardrobe changes how many and what type of pieces to plan for.
A budget ceiling directly limits the number of pieces, the brands to target, and whether to prioritise investment pieces or affordable basics.
Gender expression and body preferences (e.g. dresses only, no skirts, menswear-leaning) fundamentally shape which garment categories are relevant.
A preferred colour palette or neutral anchor colours determine which pieces will actually mix and match cohesively across the capsule.
Whether the user wants a shopping list, outfit formulas, a visual mood board, or a step-by-step sourcing plan changes the output format entirely.
The target number of outfits or pieces defines when the capsule is truly 'complete' and guides how many items need to be planned.

gold.taskTitle: Build a capsule wardrobe for the office
gold.taskDescription: Curate a small, versatile collection of work-appropriate clothing items that can be mixed and matched for daily office wear.

questions.title: What is the dress code at your workplace?
questions.description: Establish the formality level — e.g. business formal, business casual, smart casual, or creative — to define which garment categories belong in the capsule.

questions.title: Are you starting from scratch or filling wardrobe gaps?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a full build from zero or an audit-and-fill exercise based on pieces already owned.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this capsule?
questions.description: Set a spending ceiling to guide the number of pieces, brand tier, and whether to prioritise investment staples or budget-friendly basics.

questions.title: What styles or silhouettes do you feel most confident wearing?
questions.description: Capture gender expression, garment preferences (e.g. trousers over skirts, tailored over relaxed), and any items the user actively wants to avoid.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred colour palette or anchor neutrals?
questions.description: Identify the core colours that will anchor the capsule and ensure every piece can be mixed and matched cohesively.

questions.title: What format do you want the final plan delivered in?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs a shopping list, outfit formula guide, visual mood board, or a step-by-step sourcing checklist.

questions.title: How many distinct outfits should the capsule cover?
questions.description: Define the target number of outfits or total pieces so there is a clear finish line for when the capsule is complete.
